title: Field ops collision & escape plays — seller pocket binder (WIP)
content:
Purpose: compact, actionable cheat-cards + 30s/3min seller scripts for field engineers and SEs when pilots collide (capacity/routing/model mismatches) — keep customer calm, buy time, enable fallback.

Context notes (quick):
- Customers running multi-model pilot across Dedicated + Hosted; routing policy collision triggered when traffic spikes and model variant mismatches occur.
- Typical symptoms: 5xx spikes on embed endpoints, visible latency regression on chat canary, billing noise due to duplicate retries, customer sees 2x cost.
- Goal: provide repeatable plays to: 1) stabilize UX, 2) recover with graceful fallbacks, 3) preserve evidence for postmort.

Core play cards (one-liners sellers can use):
1) "Fast stabilize" (30s):
   - Say: "We see an autoscaling collision on your reserved pool. Short fix: route critical traffic to a verified lower-cost model variant while we preserve your SLA. I'll flip routing for 15 minutes and monitor."
   - Tech action: flip routing policy to weight 80/20 favoring fallback model, enable short TTL cache bypass, throttle non-critical routes.
   - Signals: 95th latency drops, error-rate down.

2) "Canary rollback" (3min):
   - Say: "Canary rollout is misbehaving — we can rollback to last-known-good model and re-run the canary with adjusted token limits."
   - Tech action: promote previous model version in rollout config, reduce canary traffic to 1%, increase sampling for debug traces.
   - Notes: capture KV-cache hit-rate before rollback.

3) "Cost quicksave" (1min):
   - Say: "We'll enable prefix caching + lower-precision quantized variant for bulk batch calls to immediately shave cost while preserving top-line results."
   - Tech action: toggle batch window to 20ms for bulk embeddings, enable quantized-variant routing for non-latency-critical endpoints.

Emergency checklist (for SE running the call) — TL;DR version:
- Step 0: acknowledge customer impact, commit to ETA for next update (15m).
- Step 1: identify topology (hosted vs dedicated vs private), note exact model ID/version and route tag.
- Step 2: check capacity dashboard (console -> model -> capacity) for throttles / OOMs.
- Step 3: apply one of core plays, depending on symptom profile.
- Step 4: open jitter log + request traces, attach to ticket INF-3421 or create new if none.
- Step 5: follow up with postmort draft and 2 action items.

Troubleshooting heuristics (quick tech checks):
- If 5xx with OOM on GPU nodes -> suspect large batch or KV cache miss. Try reducing batch_size or enabling prefix caching.
- If latency jumps but no errors -> check autoscale cold start; route to smaller-seq-length model variant.
- If cost spike + duplicate requests -> verify client-side retry policy; suggest rate-limit header + idempotency key.

Quick config snippets (ops-safe):
- Temporary routing weight change: set route.policy.weights = {"fallback-v2": 0.8, "primary": 0.2} (15m)
- Canary quick rollback: rollout.setStableVersion(model: "my-model@2026-01-14")
- Cache bypass toggle (for repro): cache.prefix_ttl = 0 -> reproduce; restore to 300s after.

Sample slide flow for a 6-slide "escape play" mini-deck (for SE handoff):
1) Title: "Pilot rescue — immediate containment" (1 slide)
2) Impact snapshot: top 3 customer metrics + timeline (1 slide)
3) Chosen play + script (1 slide)
4) Runbook: step-by-step ops actions (1 slide)
5) Short-term metrics to validate (1 slide)
6) Postmort ask + owner + next steps (1 slide)

Phrases to avoid / rebuttals:
- Avoid technical blame: don’t say "your model caused" — instead: "routing interaction across model variants caused transient pressure; here's short fix."
- If asked about reliability guarantees: defer to SLA team and frame as "we're mitigating impact and will propose a durable config change in the postmort."

Open questions / TODOs (collab notes):
- Add play variants for Private (air-gapped) deployments — current config toggles may not apply. @Priya to prototype commands.
- Validate exact console paths for routing weight edits (screenshot needed). @Jordan to add.
- Create a shorter 1-page printable "wallet card" for field events.

Links & evidence anchors:
- Related incident template: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=123456
- Jira cluster: INF-3421 (ongoing research on routing collision)
- Ops runbook repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/87

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this hyper-actionable; sellers want lines they can literally read on a call.
- Avoid deep engineering detail; give 1-2 commands they can ask an engineer to run.
- Build a quick A/B script for demonstrating rollback impact to C-level (latency + cost delta snapshot).

End of draft — use as working source for 1) seller quickplay card, 2) 6-slide rescue mini-deck, 3) small-run printable wallet card.
